record.original_question: Let Σ be an alphabet, kin [1, 2], and win Σ* be a k-power-free word. Then, in any case, w is a factor of some maximal k-power-free word over Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite alphabet and let Σ* denote the set of all finite words over Σ. For a real number k ≥ 1, a word u ∈ Σ* is called a k-power if u = v^k in the usual fractional-exponent sense (i.e., u is a prefix of v^∞ of length k|v| for some nonempty v ∈ Σ*, when k|v| is an integer; more generally u has period |v| and length k|v|). A word w ∈ Σ* is k-power-free if no factor of w is a k-power. A k-power-free word w ∈ Σ* is called maximal (over Σ) if for every letter a ∈ Σ, neither aw nor wa is k-power-free, i.e., w cannot be extended on either side while preserving k-power-freeness.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every k ∈ [1, 2] and every k-power-free word w ∈ Σ*, w is a factor of some maximal k-power-free word over Σ.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is listed as a conjecture in the WORDS conferences open problems compilation. Searches did not surface a published proof or disproof; related work (e.g., on transition properties of cube-free words and extendability of power-free words) addresses adjacent questions but does not appear to settle this specific conjecture for all k ∈ [1,2].

status_evidence.snippet: Compilation of open problems from WORDS conferences including conjectures on maximal k-power-free words.
status_evidence.claim: The statement is recorded as an open conjecture in the WORDS conferences open-problems list.

status_evidence.title: Transition Property For Cube-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Studies extension and transition properties of cube-free words.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent results on extendability of power-free words exist but do not resolve the conjecture as stated for all k in [1,2].
